pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented at 00:21:09 — three to four sessions a week, 30 to 40 minutes, strength, conditioning and mobility in every session, plus five-to-ten-minute daily mobility protocols aimed at his desk work, and the teach-you-everything-in-six-months framing. Asked 'does this kind of approach, do you feel like that would work for you?' he answered 'Yeah, sounds good.' Understood and agreed, no questions, no elaboration.

Presented at 00:23:00 as what/when/how much with an eight-hour eating window, no tracking, and a weekly pizza. Asked 'Do you have any questions in terms of nutrition?' he answered 'Not at moment, no.' Notable non-event: the prospect had explicitly said he deliberately reintroduced carbs as a fuel source and eats a 'whole holistic plate', and the rep neither engaged with that nor flagged any tension with the eight-hour window. Nothing was contested because nothing was examined.

The only pillar he tied to himself unprompted: 'So I think on the holistic side of things, it sounds good. I like the approach, obviously, training, nutrition, accountability. For me personally, probably the accountability is a big part.' He also echoed the rep's phrasing back — 'No more, no more on and off' / 'Locked in' — which is the one moment of genuine energy in the presentation. This is the pillar the sale rests on and the rep correctly identified it as such.

anchors.raw: if I have like a home setup, which I currently do in my garage, it was the most cost-effective as well as easiest thing to start with.
anchors.note: He chose kettlebells specifically on cost-effectiveness grounds and has already bought the equipment and built the garage gym. His reference point for solving this problem is a few hundred dollars of hardware plus free online programming, which is the frame $6,000 lands into. The rep never repositioned the spend from equipment to coaching.

anchors.raw: I was trying to find this online, but I wasn't able to. So, what are the actual costs?
anchors.note: He arrived with no anchor at all because none is published, and asked for price in his opening breath. Absent an external reference he substituted his own — 'It's definitely a big amount' — with nothing to compare it against. The absence of an anchor is not neutral here: it left the number to be judged in isolation forty minutes before he had a comparison.

unmet_demand.want: A clear, complete picture of the payment options so he could evaluate them as an accountant
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The option set was delivered incompletely and the arithmetic was left unstated. The monthly figure of $1,200 was given without the $7,200 total it implies, the half-split was mentioned without amounts or dates, and the third-party financing sentence was cut off mid-delivery — 'you could even split it up, up to' — and never finished. He was asked to make a decision on numbers he had not fully received.

unmet_demand.want: Support that extends to his wife, who is two months post-partum, newly cleared for light exercise and part of the same household pattern he is trying to break
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised her twice and described their weight gain as a shared cycle they had repeatedly tried and failed to break together. The programme is one-to-one male coaching and there was no partner, household or referral pathway offered. The rep's response placed the burden back on him — 'that's actually on you. I mean, you need to put in the effort also for her.'
